tweets.text:
When the market is ripping you have to accept that the "clean" high time frame retests you want may never come.  

If they do happen, it's usually after price has already extended significantly to the upside. 

There will still be spots where we get large corrections but they are few and far between and require patience and a belief in your bias not to get bearish during them.

Active trading should be focused on lower timeframes and you need to stop assuming every move is going to immediately mean revert as in prior price regimes. 

Lastly, you need to decide if you are willing to buy things that have already broken out with momentum and risk buying a top before a pullback or wait for those high time frame retest and risk being sidelined.

tweets.text:
At no point anywhere have I claimed that I sniped the bottom. 

If you actually follow the stuff I say via telegram, twitter and youtube I've been pretty clear for the last few months.

As recent as yesterday I said above $67.2k I think we trade into the mid $70ks. 

I personally have been a 4 year cycle believer, meaning a Q4 bottom. With that being said, I believed we'd been trading in an area where I believe Bitcoin is good long term value.

My plan has and continues to be to accumulate while leaving some dry powder in case of a longer accumulation period or another low with the goal of being fully allocated by the end of the year. 

Ultimate confirmation for me that the low is in would be a weekly market structure break to the upside, just like the last bear market low.

Trading is about having strong opinions and holding them loosely. When presented with new information, like a 20% candle to the upside, you need to ignore your ego about bottom ticking and be willing to adapt 

I was lucky enough to scoop some Bitcoin near the lows but didn't full port at what appears to be the bottom as that was never my plan.
